blockNote: Player-actor transition scripts plus one impact effect (Bank 00, 50200-50671). Most routines are not run by an actor of their own: a caller (scene script, item code, warp code) writes a routine's address into the player actor's entry pointer ($0000,Y low word and $0002,Y bank byte), clears the player's wait counter ($0008,Y), and the player actor runs the routine on its next turn (X = D = the player slot, so every COP inside acts on the player). The routines hold a pose, play a short sequence or give control back; most finish with JML player_character.PlayerIdleEntry, which also clears playerFlags $2800, so the $0800 script lock set by the caller or the routine is released there.
=== ENTRY POINTS AND CALLERS (from the pointer writes) ===

- player_transition_handlers (50200): SpawnListAppend PlayerItemRevealSpawn, then Die. It is the default script written into an actor hit by the player's interaction / push strike (combat_collision.ApplyHitDamageToVictim path 1, together with $10 |= $0040) and is reached by JumpFar from gw8A_sand_fanger (756178).

- PlayerItemRevealSpawn (50211): effect actor: SFX $09, frame $2A of spriteset_enemies, then Die. Spawned by player_transition_handlers and by gw82_archer (SpawnListAppend at X +- 14, Y - 14, flags $0302), so it is an impact spark, not an item reveal (OQ-I052-9).
- PlayerIdleAnimLoop (50226): idle animation loop. Callers: warps_interaction (while the music upload finishes) and ir29_castoth func_0AA37B.
- PlayerStaticBodyPose / PlayerWalkingIdlePose (50246 / 50261): the flute playback in item_use_system holds body 4 frame $1F, then restores control.
- RestorePlayerControlDirect (50266): JML PlayerIdleEntry. Callers: warps_interaction and ir29_castoth func_0AA391.

- PlayerFreedanRevealIdle / PlayerFreedanRevealExit (50270 / 50285): hold body 4 frame $20 (every frame / once, then PlayerIdleEntry). Idle: gs2D_lily, gs2E_sleep, dc2F_adrift, dc31_rescuer. Exit: dc31_kara. The callers give no support for the name Freedan (OQ-I052-2).
- PlayerIdleEntryJump (50281): a bare JML PlayerIdleEntry; no reference found.
- PlayerFallFromHeight (50297): awBD_fall_trigger. PlayerSkyGardenJumpLanding (50385): sg4D_jump_handler. PlayerAuraTransformEntry (50519): item_use_system.UseItem_Aura (Shadow only, standing still).
=== FLAG BITS USED ===

Player actor flags $10: $0008 = normal collision-aware movement (cleared while a script moves the player, set again at the end), $0200 = scripted motion marker (the Psycho Slider and the lunge set it too), $2000 = SortActorsByDepth skips the actor and PlayerIdleEntry yields without acting (meaning open: OQ-I025-2), $0040 = death flag. playerFlags $0800 = script / ability lock. layerPriorityFlag ($06EE) bit $0200 = camera frozen (the old comment called it 'force layer priority'). joypadMaskStd |= $CFFC hides every button except Select / Start (the old comment said $CFF0).
The old header's 'item reveal with metasprite staging' is the PlayerItemRevealSpawn spark.

partNotes.player_transition_handlers: Default victim script and spark spawner: spawn PlayerItemRevealSpawn at this actor (offsets 0, 0, flags $0302) and Die. See the block note for how an actor ends up here.
partNotes.PlayerItemRevealSpawn: Impact spark actor: SFX $09 on channel 2, frame $2A of spriteset_enemies, AnimOnce, Die. The code after the Die belongs to the same block but is only entered through the entry pointer written into the player actor.
partNotes.PlayerIdleAnimLoop: Entered as the player's script. When per-scene flag #00 is set it stages anim $11 (PlayerIdleUseShadowSprite), otherwise anim $01, then loops AnimOnce until the caller redirects the player. What flag #00 means is open (OQ-I052-1).
partNotes.PlayerIdleUseShadowSprite: Per-scene flag #00 set: stage anim $11 instead of $01.
partNotes.PlayerIdleAnimContinue: Loop: SetEntryHere, AnimOnce, repeat. Each pass saves the loop as the re-entry point and plays the animation once.
partNotes.PlayerStaticBodyPose: Flute pose: $10 |= $0200, body table index 4 (SetPlayerSpriteDirect), then frame $1F is staged again on every pass. item_use_system writes this as the player's script while the melody plays.
partNotes.PlayerStaticBodyAnimLoop: Stage frame $1F and play it once, forever.
partNotes.PlayerWalkingIdlePose: End of the flute: clear $10 bit $0200 and fall into RestorePlayerControlDirect.
partNotes.PlayerFreedanRevealIdle: Hold pose: body table index 4, then every frame stage frame $20 and play it once (SetEntryHere + RTL). The callers place the player first (gs2E_sleep also moves it up 8 px).
partNotes.PlayerFreedanRevealExit: Leave the held pose: body 4 frame $20 once, then PlayerIdleEntry.
partNotes.PlayerFallFromHeight: Fall into the scene (awBD_fall_trigger): hide the buttons, lock the player, leave collision-aware movement, freeze the camera; 3 frames out of the depth sort, Y -= 128, then 8 passes of fall anim $19 with Y chain 7 (+4 px per frame), landing SFX $2C and frame $1C. Then restore $10 / camera / buttons and return to PlayerIdleEntry (which clears the $0800 lock). Whether the fall ends exactly on the original Y is not checked: OQ-I052-3.
partNotes.PlayerSkyGardenJumpLanding: Jump sequence of sg4D_jump_handler (the caller sets playerFlags $0800): leave collision-aware movement, $10 |= $2200, Y -= 64, freeze the camera, 3 frames, Y += 64, show the player, flip the sprite vertically, Y -= 32 and rise with decelerating Y chains (8 x4 passes, 4 x2, 2 x2); flip back, Y += 32, descend (chains 1, 3), landing SFX $2C and frame $1F; restore $10 and the camera and return to PlayerIdleEntry. The buttons are not masked or unmasked here.
partNotes.PlayerAuraTransformEntry: Aura (item_use_system.UseItem_Aura, Shadow standing still): lock the player, leave collision-aware movement, $10 |= $0200, body table index 8, frame 0; save X / Y in $24 / $26, align Y to a 16 px row, then search for floor (PlayerAuraAlignToSolidSouth). The terrain type $04 test below decides between the sink and an abort (OQ-I052-4).
partNotes.PlayerAuraAlignToSolidSouth: Scan down one 16 px row at a time until BranchIfSolidHere reports a blocked tile; the whole scan runs inside one frame.
partNotes.PlayerAuraBlockedBySolid: Blocked tile found: when the tile below (Y + 16) has terrain type $04 go to PlayerAuraDescendToFloor; otherwise restore the saved position, show frame 1 once and leave through PlayerAuraTransformExit.
partNotes.PlayerAuraDescendToFloor: Restore the saved X / Y, set $10 bit $2000 and sink: PlayerAuraScanSolidRow.
partNotes.PlayerAuraScanSolidRow: Every 16th pixel row test for terrain type $04 at the actor position; on a match land.
partNotes.PlayerAuraScanSolidNext: Sink 1 px and continue next frame (JumpNextFrame).
partNotes.PlayerAuraLandOnSolid: Type $04 reached: clear $2000, set $10 bit $0002 (meaning open: OQ-I052-5) and slide down with sprite anim 2 / Y chain 1 (+1 px per frame) until the tile type at the actor is 0.
partNotes.PlayerAuraLandAnimLoop: One pass of the landing slide: anim 2, +1 px per frame, then test the tile type.
partNotes.PlayerAuraLandComplete: Open tile reached: clear $10 bit $0002, show frame $1C (anim $1C, no movement) and fall into PlayerAuraTransformExit.
partNotes.PlayerAuraTransformExit: End: normal movement again ($10 |= $0008, clear $0200), no pending wait, PlayerIdleEntry (clears the $0800 lock).

blockNote: Room-reveal effect (Bank 00, 56818-57107): after the enemy that guards a hidden room part is defeated, a glowing sprite rises from the corpse, flies to the centre of the revealed region, flashes, scatters ten sparkles and swaps the background tiles (StageBgChangeFromDeathIdx + ApplyBgChange). Three actor bodies live in this file: SpawnFieldRevealEffect, field_reveal_scatter (which falls through into field_reveal_flash) and field_reveal_flash.
=== SPAWN ===

SpawnListAppend ( SpawnFieldRevealEffect, #00, #00, #$0342 ) in StandardEnemyDefeatHandler (56375), EnemyDefeatDispatch_CountKill (697548), pyCC_mystic_ball (771970) and awB1_wall_walker (770414). The spawner copies its deathActionIdx ($7F0024, the event-block index of its scene record) into the child; EnemyDefeatDispatch_CountKill guards the spawn with event flag $0100 + index so each reveal fires once.
=== TARGET ===

event_block_table is indexed by deathActionIdx x 8. The bytes used are +3 width, +4 height, +5 dstX and +6 dstY (event-block-def, tile units). The flight target is the centre of the destination rectangle in pixels: moveXAlt = (2 x dstX + width) x 8, moveYAlt = (2 x dstY + height) x 8. orbitAngle := width / 2 and orbitDiameter := height / 2 are passed to the scatter particles as their range tier.
=== SEQUENCE ===

Flags $0342, palette 0, anim $29: three rising passes (Y chains $02, $12, $14), a two-pass hover loop, sprite priority $30, then StageMove to the target at 4 px per frame (TickMove). On arrival: a field_reveal_flash child, a 1-frame wait, $10 |= $2000, then ten field_reveal_scatter children (one every 3 frames; each gets the half-width and half-height), then StageBgChangeFromDeathIdx (SFX $0F on both channels, stages the swap), ApplyBgChange and Die. Each child gets $12 |= $1000 (the display / overlay-active qualifier, which CopyActorState clears).
The old header named an 'Incan Ruins wind trap' as a user (the four callers above are the real ones) and called +3 / +5 the 'target X tile' and 'X size'; they are the width and dstX.

partNotes.SpawnFieldRevealEffect: Main actor of the reveal: rise, fly to the centre of the event-block rectangle, flash, ten scatter sparkles, background swap, Die. See the block note.
field_reveal_scatter: Scatter sparkle (child of SpawnFieldRevealEffect): offsets its own position by a random amount per axis. $20 = half-width and $22 = half-height in tiles. X magnitude: $20 >= 4 gives 0-63 px, 2-3 gives 0-31, 0-1 gives 0-15. Y: $22 >= 3 gives 0-63, 2 gives 0-31, 0-1 gives 0-15 (the Y thresholds differ from the X ones). The random byte is shifted right once and the carry is the sign (set = negative).
There is no Die at the end: the code runs on into field_reveal_flash, so every sparkle also plays SFX $06 on both channels, shows frame $25 and then dies.

partNotes.loc_00DEDC: Random Y offset: tiers from $22 (>= 3, 2, below).
partNotes.loc_00DEF5: Y range tier 3 or more: magnitude 0-63 px.
partNotes.loc_00DEFF: Apply the sign (carry from the LSR) to the Y offset.
partNotes.loc_00DF05: Add the Y offset; the sparkle continues into field_reveal_flash.
partNotes.field_reveal_flash: Flash: SFX $06 on both channels, frame $25 once, Die. Spawned once at the arrival point by SpawnFieldRevealEffect and also the tail of every scatter sparkle.

blockNote: Escort follower actor (Bank 00, 51206-51522; the delta table follows): spawned as a child of an escort NPC (Kara / Lily), it records the player's path and replays it on the NPC, so the NPC walks the player's route about 8 recorded frames behind.
=== SPAWN AND PARAMETERS ===

SpawnAfterFlags ( EscortFollowPathTracker, #$2000 ) (#$2800 in btDE_kara_missing) in ec0A_kara, it1A_lily, ir1C_lily, eu97_clerk2, btDF_kara, btDE_kara_missing and btE3_kara. The child sits right behind its parent in the actor list, so its $04 (prevActorLink) is the NPC. The spawner sets orbitAngle = initial facing + 1 (Lily: 4, so facing 3) or 0 (use the player's current facing), and orbitDiameter = the NPC's base animation index (Lily: $1A).
=== RING BUFFER at $7EDF00 ===

Eight-byte entries: X word, Y word, facing word, unused. The setup writes 9 entries (offsets $00-$40): a trail that starts at the NPC and steps 2 px per entry along the table row of the facing index. The row is the OPPOSITE direction and the entry's facing word the opposite facing (EscortFollowPathDeltaTable: facing 0 South steps Y -2, 1 North Y +2, 2 West X +2, 3 East X -2). Only 8 entries are ever read: every access masks orbitAngle with $3F, so the byte offset runs $00-$38 and the ninth entry ($7EDF40) is unreachable. No other code uses $7EDF00.
=== PER FRAME (after SetEntryHereAndYield) ===
Own $14 / $16 = the player's position of the last frame, $0E = the facing last applied to the NPC, orbitAngle = ring head (byte offset).

- Player moved: the NPC jumps to the head entry (written 8 recorded frames ago), the head entry is overwritten with the player's current X / Y, and when the head entry's facing differs from $0E the NPC gets animation orbitDiameter + facing + 4 ($28; $2A and $08 cleared). Then the head entry's facing is refreshed with the player's current facing and the head advances by 8.

- Player still: the NPC shows animation orbitDiameter + facing of the head entry (no +4); its position is untouched, the head does not advance and $0E := $FFFF so the next move restarts the walk animation.

Edge: GetPlayerFacingDirection returns carry set and A >= 4 for an unknown facing; the table index then runs past the four rows (OQ-I052-7). The old header said '9-waypoint ring buffer' and 'each frame advances orbitAngle by 8'; the head advances only on frames where the player moved, and the first use of orbitAngle is a seed, not a timer.

partNotes.EscortFollowPathTracker: Setup (the frame after the spawn): pick the table row from the seed or the player's facing, lay the 9-entry trail from the NPC's position, copy the player's position into $14 / $16, orbitAngle := 0, SetEntryHereAndYield. The per-frame body follows. See the block note.
